blockNote: Mode 7 perspective thinker (Bank 03, 239936-240520). Every frame it rebuilds three 224-line HDMA tables that drive the Mode 7 matrix registers M7A-M7D, so the flat Mode 7 plane is rotated by an angle index and gets a perspective gradient (the zoom grows from the top scanline to the bottom one).
=== ENTRY POINTS ===

- Mode7PerspectiveInit is a thinker-def <#04,#08>: the two header bytes are the word $0804 that goes into animScratch2. Bit 2 puts the thinker into RunThinkers_TypeB, which runs after ResetHdmaState every frame; the four HDMA channels queued below are therefore re-armed each frame. Bit 11 is the lighter-frame flag. Only the scene thinker list of scene $FE (the world map, thinker_spawn_0CEB3D = Init + IrisCircleEffect) spawns it through the list.
- Init has no RTL: it falls straight into Mode7PerspectiveUpdate (the Update block starts at the byte after Init's last STA).

- Four actor scripts spawn Mode7PerspectiveUpdate directly with COP SpawnThinker and skip Init: pr8C_prologue1 and pr8C_prologue5 (prologue prophecy), garden_crash_cutscene (Sky Garden crash) and future_vision_cutscene (Angkor Wat). SpawnThinker does not read the thinker-def header, so each of them stores $0804 into the new thinker's animScratch2 itself, writes M7SEL = 0 (map repeats) and drives the three parameters below from a companion script.
=== PARAMETERS (global low-RAM words, not actor fields) ===
The thinker reads absolute low-RAM words (D is forced to 0), so every script writes them with STA $00B8 style absolute stores. They are not per-thinker fields.
| Word | Role here | Written by |

| $00B8 | Starting divisor ('scale'). The quotient is abs(cos) / divisor in 8.8 fixed point, so $80 is about 1:1 ($7FFF / $80 = $FF), a smaller divisor zooms out and a larger one zooms in. Init sets $0400 | Cutscene controllers (future vision $001C up to $0080, prologue $0020), WorldMapController (adds gravity deltas) |

| $00B6 | Divisor increment per scanline, 8.8 fixed point. 0 gives a flat plane without perspective. Init sets 0 | Prologue controllers ($0280 / $0200 counted down towards 0), future vision (INC), WorldMapController (descent loop subtracts $10 per frame) |

| $00BC | Rotation index. ($BC AND $01FF) x 2 indexes the 512-step sine and cosine tables (0.703 degrees per step). Init sets 0 | Cutscenes INC it; WorldMapController route steps add their third delta axis to it (its own comments call that axis elevation) |
| $00CA / $00CC | Mode 7 centre X / Y (copied to M7X / M7Y by the NMI). Init takes them from worldMapPlayerX / Y ($0D54 / $0D56) | Init, the cutscene controllers, WorldMapController |
=== ONE-TIME TABLE FILL ===

The first tick writes 224 entries of {count 1, data word 0} plus a $00 terminator into $7E7000 (M7A), $7E7800 (M7B) and $7E8000 (M7C): 673 bytes each. A count of 1 with bit 7 clear is a one-scanline, non-repeat entry. COP SetEntryHere follows, so only the data words are rewritten on later frames.
=== PER-FRAME COMPUTATION ===
1. D := 0. Scratch is absolute $00-$04, $0E, $18 and $1C. $00/$01 := 0 (this clears the fraction byte $01), $02 := $B8 (the divisor word $02/$03), $04 := $B6, $0E := 224.

2. Y = ($BC AND $1FF) x 2. cos is read from cosine_table_16bit[Y] and sin from sine_table_16bit[Y] ($7FFF = 1.0). Both tables are read past their nominal length on purpose (math_lookup_tables adjacency contract). The absolute values go to $18 (|cos|) and $1C (|sin|); the two signs choose one of four routines.
3. PEA QueueMode7HdmaTables-1 makes the routine's final RTS continue in the queue code (return-address trick).
4. NormalizeDivisor shifts $02, $18, $1C and $04 right together until the divisor word has no high byte. The quotients do not change; the 8-bit WRDIVB divisor input is satisfied.

5. For each of the 224 scanlines: divide |cos| by the divisor with the hardware 16/8 divider, divide |sin|, store the signed results into the three tables, then add $04 to the 16-bit word at $01/$02. $01 is the fraction byte and $02 the low byte of the divisor word, so this adds $B6 / 256 to the divisor: the divisor, and with it the zoom, grows down the screen.

6. If that add carries out of $02, the carry is added to $03 and |cos|, |sin|, the divisor word and $04 are all halved. Their ratios are kept and the divisor returns to 8 bits. The fraction byte $01 is not halved.
| +cos, +sin | +cos/div | +sin/div | -sin/div |
| +cos, -sin | +cos/div | -abs(sin)/div | +abs(sin)/div |
| -cos, +sin | -abs(cos)/div | +sin/div | -sin/div |
| -cos, -sin | -abs(cos)/div | -abs(sin)/div | +abs(sin)/div |
In every case A = D = cos/div, B = sin/div and C = -sin/div: the rotation matrix divided by the per-scanline divisor.
=== HDMA QUEUE ===

QueueMode7HdmaTables issues four COP QueueDma. The second operand is a B-bus register index (#1B..#1E = $211B..$211E), not a channel number. QueueDma sets up a DIRECT-table HDMA channel on the next free channel (cop_handlers_hdma_dma), so four channels are used per frame and released again by the next ResetHdmaState. Table A is queued twice, for M7A and for M7D.
=== QUIRKS ===

- M7SEL = $80 written by Init means: tilemap repeat off and non-tilemap fill = 0, i.e. the area outside the 1024x1024 map is transparent (nesdev PPU registers). The old notes said 'repeat'. The cutscene spawners write M7SEL = 0 instead, which repeats the map.
- $B6 is the per-scanline divisor increment, not a rotation angle; the rotation is $BC.
- STY $WRDIVB with 16-bit Y also writes $4207 (HTIMEL) with the divisor high byte, which is 0 here. No H-IRQ use was checked.
- Quadrants 3 and 4 use 4 NOPs where 1 and 2 use 6: the extra LDA #0 / SEC before the SBC fill the divider's 16-cycle delay (derived from cycle counts, not run).
- The three tables live at $7E7000, $7E7800 and $7E8000, the same addresses as tileStagingBuffer and as buffers of parallax_thinker. No check was made for scenes that use both (OQ-I041-3).
- Init writes $FFFF to the words $7F0B22 and $7F0B24. No reader was found in extracted/ (OQ-I041-1).

Mode7PerspectiveInit: Thinker entry for scene $FE only. M7SEL := $80; $7F0B22 and $7F0B24 := $FFFF; Mode 7 centre := world-map start position; camera := centre - ($80, $70) with the bit 15 scroll-override flag; $B6 := 0, $BC := 0, $B8 := $0400. Falls through into Mode7PerspectiveUpdate.
Mode7PerspectiveUpdate: Table fill (first tick only) followed by the per-frame matrix computation. Entered by fall-through from Init (scene $FE) or directly as the SpawnThinker target of the prologue, Sky Garden crash and Angkor Wat vision scripts. COP SetEntryHere separates the one-time fill from the per-frame part.

Per frame: scratch $02 := $B8 (divisor), $04 := $B6 (increment), index Y := ($BC AND $1FF) x 2, then cos and sin from the 16-bit tables, absolute values in $18 and $1C, jump to the matching quadrant routine with QueueMode7HdmaTables-1 on the stack.
loc_03A994: Fill loop: one entry per scanline in all three tables (count byte 1, data bytes left 0), 224 times, then $00 terminators.
loc_03A9F0: cos >= 0 and sin < 0: negate sin and enter the second quadrant routine.
loc_03A9F9: cos < 0: negate cos, re-read sin and choose the third or fourth quadrant routine.
loc_03AA09: cos < 0 and sin < 0: negate sin and enter the fourth quadrant routine.
QueueMode7HdmaTables: RTS-trick return target. Restores D and the thinker slot, then queues four direct-table HDMA transfers: table A to M7A ($211B), B to M7B ($211C), C to M7C ($211D) and A again to M7D ($211E). Ends with RTL back to the thinker loop.
Mode7Quadrant_PosCosPosSin: Quadrant 1 (+cos, +sin). NormalizeDivisor, then 224 scanlines: A := cos/div, B := sin/div, C := -(sin/div), divisor += $B6/256. Carry out of the accumulator halves everything (loc_03AA6F).
loc_03AA30: Scanline loop of quadrant 1: two divides, three table writes, divisor accumulation.
loc_03AA6F: Quadrant 1 overflow: add the carry to the divisor high byte, halve |cos|, |sin|, the divisor word and the increment, and continue the loop.
Mode7Quadrant_PosCosNegSin: Quadrant 2 (+cos, -sin). Same as quadrant 1 but the sin quotient goes to table C unchanged and its negation to table B, so B = sin/div (negative) and C = -sin/div (positive).
Mode7Quadrant_NegCosPosSin: Quadrant 3 (-cos, +sin). A := 0 - cos/div, B := sin/div, C := -(sin/div). Uses 4 NOPs because the LDA #0 / SEC / SBC read delays the RDDIVL access.
NormalizeDivisor: Shift the divisor word, |cos|, |sin| and the increment right together until the divisor high byte is zero, so the divisor fits the 8-bit WRDIVB register. The ratios, and therefore the quotients, are unchanged.
loc_03AB7D: Shift step of NormalizeDivisor: A = divisor >> 1, then $18, $1C and $04 shifted too, and test again.

blockNote: Floating damage-number actor (Bank 00, 56500-56579). One spawn is one 16-frame effect: it draws the damage value as digit sprites above the victim and lets them rise one pixel per frame while following the victim's own movement. The name 'attack trail' and the old text ('ghost copies interpolated between the previous and current position', '16 frames at position then 16 drifting upward', 'when the player or enemies take damage') do not describe it: there is one 16-iteration loop and no ghost copies.
=== SPAWN ===

Two sites in combat_collision: COP SpawnListAppend ( @SpawnAttackTrailEffect, #00, #00, flags ) in PlayerAttackHitTest with flags $2F00, and in ApplyHitDamageToVictim_DamagePath with flags $2B00 (that path then ORs $1000 into the child's $12). The fourth operand is the flags word stored into the child's $10, not a priority. Both sites run with the victim as the current actor, so CopyActorState gives the child the victim's X and Y and stores the victim's slot in the child's $24. The caller then writes the packed BCD damage from FormatDamageDigits into the child's $28.
No child is spawned when the victim's $12 bit $0020 (boss) is set or when the damage is 1000 or more (FormatDamageDigits returns carry). No other spawn site exists in extracted/.
=== BODY ===
1. $0E := $3200: the attribute word ORed into every digit tile (OAM high byte $32 = priority 3, palette 1).
2. $16 -= $10: start 16 pixels above the victim.
3. Y := $24 (the victim); remember its X and Y in $20 and $22.

4. 16 iterations (LoopStart #10 = 16): add the victim's X movement since last frame to $14, add its Y movement minus 1 to $16 (so the digits rise one pixel per frame), refresh $20/$22, copy $28 to the absolute scratch word $0000 and call ComposeDigitSprites. ComposeDigitSprites puts the first digit at $14 - 12 and appends one 6-byte entry per digit to the compose buffer at $7F3100. LoopEnd yields every iteration, so the digits are re-emitted every frame; then Die.
The scratch word is written with the absolute address $0000 on purpose: it is not the actor's own $00/$01 re-entry address.
=== HAZARD ===

The loop re-reads the victim's position through $24 every frame and never checks that the slot still holds the same actor. If the victim died and its slot were reused within the 16 frames, the number would follow whatever occupies the slot (analysis only, not run; OQ-I041-5).
AttackTrailShort_unused is an unreferenced variant of this routine.

SpawnAttackTrailEffect: Entry of the child actor created by SpawnListAppend. $24 = victim slot, $28 = packed BCD damage (written by the caller after the spawn), $14/$16 = victim position at spawn.

blockNote: Hidden Red Jewel pickup (Bank 00, 50802-50853 plus two dialog strings): a small interactable that gives item $01 (Red Jewel) once and remembers it in a persistent event flag. The same file also holds HiddenRedJewelInventoryFull, which seven NPC scripts jump into for their own 'jewel gift but inventory full' message.
=== SPAWN AND FLAG ===

actor-def <#00,#00,#30>. The spawn record's odd type byte is shifted right by one into $0E (the actor never overwrites it). Sixteen placements exist, one per scene, with $0E = 0..F, so the flag index $0E + $80 runs over $80..$8F on the event-flag base $0200 (flags $0280-$028F, bytes $0A50-$0A51; chests use the lower indices of the same base):
| Scene | Area | Type byte | $0E |
| 03 | south_cape/lances_house | 01 | 0 |
| 01 | south_cape/south_cape | 03 | 1 |
| 13 | edward_castle/aqueduct_exit | 05 | 2 |
| 15 | itory/itory_village | 07 | 3 |
| 30 | freejia/oakton | 09 | 4 |
| 39 | freejia/freejia_hotel | 0B | 5 |
| 6C | angel_village/angel_rooms | 0D | 6 |
| 74 | angel_village/angel_tunnel_rooms | 0F | 7 |
| 78 | watermia/watermia | 11 | 8 |
| 7B | watermia/gambling_house | 13 | 9 |
| 91 | euro/euro | 15 | A |
| 9D | euro/dark_chapel | 17 | B |
| AE | native_village/gorgon_hut | 19 | C |
| C3 | dao/dao | 1B | D |
| CC | pyramid/pyramid_main | 1D | E |
| DF | babel_tower/babel_lower_floors | 1F | F |
The flag is not tested at spawn time: the actor is always placed and simply does nothing once its flag is set.
=== INTERACTION ===

The init script sets the interact handler, the metasprite (spriteset_enemies), sprite and hitbox config #00 and idles with SetEntryHere + RTL. HiddenRedJewelInteract: A := $0E + $80, TestEventFlag_0200. Flag set: return silently. Flag clear: COP GiveItem ( #01, &HiddenRedJewelInventoryFull ); on success print dialogstring_00C6A6 ('You found a Red Jewel!') and set the flag; if the inventory is full GiveItem branches to HiddenRedJewelInventoryFull, which prints dialogstring_00C6BF and returns without setting the flag, so the jewel can be tried again later. GiveItem itself prints nothing; the dialog is this script's own.
=== NPC JUMPS ===

gs2B_seth, nvAE_stone_girl2, wa79_lance, fr32_creep, eu95_ann, sc01_fisherman and ec0A_right_guard each end their gift script with JML @hidden_red_jewel.HiddenRedJewelInventoryFull when GiveItem reports a full inventory. They do not use the interact handler or the flag range above.
Whether the jewel is visible and what the metasprite looks like was not checked (OQ-I041-7).
